name: Baton – AI Walkthroughs, Guided Tours & Client Handover
author: Chidiebere Chukwudi

sections.description:
Handing a site over usually means a long call, a messy doc, or a screen recording nobody watches. Baton does it differently: it shows people around the actual dashboard.

You just do the task like you normally would. Add a page, update a product, change the menu. Baton watches your clicks, keeps a copy of each screen, and turns it all into a walkthrough. The next time your client logs in, they get to practise it: the screens look exactly as you recorded them, and they click the highlighted spot, one step at a time. Nothing they click there can break anything.

The steps that finish the job happen for real. When they press Publish, their post is published, with the title and words they typed. Install installs the plugin, Activate turns it on. So they learn by doing, and the work gets done too.

How it works:

  1. In your dashboard, click Baton → Record a walkthrough in the admin bar.
  2. Do the task you want to show, across as many screens as you need.
  3. Click Stop, give it a name, and let AI write the steps (or write them yourself).
  4. Click “Take the walkthrough” to try it yourself, then pick who should see it and publish.

If you did some of the steps for real while recording, like installing a plugin or making a post, Baton offers to remove them so your client can do them fresh.

What you get:

  • A practice copy of every screen, with each menu, button or box highlighted and a plain-words tip
  • Clicking the highlighted spot moves on, typing goes in the boxes, so people learn by doing
  • Publish, Install and Activate happen for real, for people allowed to do them
  • “Watch it”, to see the whole task played step by step
  • The same steps every time, whatever has changed on the site since you recorded
  • Works in the block editor too, including inside the writing area
  • AI that writes ridiculously simple steps like “Click “Pages””, “Fill in “Site title”” or “Tick “Allow comments””, and leaves out side trips like opening Help
  • Control over who sees each walkthrough (by role) and when (once, or every login until they finish)
  • A list of walkthroughs in the admin bar, so people can take them again any time
  • A preview button, so you can try any walkthrough (even a draft) before anyone else sees it, or jump to a single step
  • Works on multisite: each site keeps its own walkthroughs and progress
  • A tour link for each published walkthrough, to put on a button, a menu item or in a help doc
  • Edit, reorder (drag and drop) or remove any step

Privacy comes first:

  • Recording is only for site administrators, and only while you’ve pressed Record
  • Only clicks and a copy of each screen are saved, on your own site. Passwords are never kept in the copies
  • Clicks on Baton’s own menu are left out
  • AI is optional, and never sees anything typed

Baton Pro

Baton Pro is a paid add-on for when you want to guide more than your team. Baton works fully on its own without it.

  • Walkthroughs on the front end of your site, for customers, members and students
  • Tours for guests and visitors who aren’t logged in
  • Record inside Elementor’s editor
  • Start a tour automatically, or suggest it on the pages you choose
  • Invite-only walkthroughs, shared with a private link
  • Your own name in the dashboard menu, and no “Made with Baton”
  • Unlimited AI step writing

Learn more at baton.chidiebere.dev.

External services

Baton AI step writer

Baton connects to the Baton AI step writer, a service run by the plugin author at baton-ai.chidideveloper.workers.dev. It turns the clicks you recorded into short, plain step descriptions like “Click “Pages””. It runs on Cloudflare Workers and uses Cloudflare Workers AI to write the text.

When: only when a site administrator clicks “Save and let AI write the steps” after a recording, or “Write steps with AI” on a walkthrough’s edit screen. Nothing is sent otherwise, and you can always write the steps yourself instead.

What is sent, for every step of that walkthrough:

  • The name of the page the step was on (like “Settings › General”)
  • The kind of control that was clicked (like “button”, “link” or “checkbox”)
  • The text on that control (like “Add Page”)

When the AI writes the steps, the same service also checks the recording for side trips, like opening Help and not using it, so they can be left out. You can put them back with one click. When: only after “Save and let AI write the steps”, and only if the recording has such a click. What is sent: each step’s text, page name, kind of control and what it opened (like “menu “Options””).

Each request also carries a one-way scrambled code made from your site address (a SHA-256 hash), so the service can count each site’s daily allowance without knowing which site it is. Your server’s IP address is used to stop too many requests at once. Nothing typed into forms, no page addresses and no user details are sent.

Send feedback

Baton → Send feedback emails your message to the plugin author (from your site, using WordPress’s own email), with a screenshot if you add one. A copy of the words, without the screenshot, also goes to the same service as above, in case your site can’t send email.

When: only when you press Send on that screen. Nothing is sent otherwise.

What is sent: what you wrote, whether it’s a problem or an idea, and the email in the reply box (it starts filled in with your own, and you can change or clear it). If “Include this site’s address and versions” is ticked (you can untick it), also your site’s address and the versions of Baton, Baton Pro, WordPress, PHP, Elementor and your theme, plus the site’s language. Messages are kept for 90 days.

“How was this?” answers at the end of a walkthrough are different: they stay on your site and are never sent anywhere.

  • Terms of use: baton.chidiebere.dev/terms
  • Privacy policy: baton.chidiebere.dev/privacy
  • The service runs on Cloudflare: terms of service, privacy policy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Baton.
  2. Go to any page in your dashboard.
  3. Click Baton → Record a walkthrough in the admin bar and start clicking.
sections.faq:
Who sees a walkthrough?

Logged-in users with the roles you tick. Tick none and everyone who logs in sees it. Drafts are never shown.

When does it launch?

Right after login, in the dashboard. It opens over whatever screen they land on. You choose whether it starts straight away or asks first, and whether it shows once or at every login until they finish it.

What if a screen changes after I record?

Nothing breaks. People practise on the screens as you recorded them, so every step is always where you left it. If the real screen has changed a lot, record the walkthrough again.

What about pop-ups that only show once, like the editor’s welcome guide?

If you click one while recording, it becomes a step, and it shows in the practice just like it did for you. You can remove that step on the walkthrough’s edit screen.

Do I have to use AI?

No. AI only runs when you click “Save and let AI write the steps” or “Write steps with AI”. Otherwise, Baton writes simple steps from the button and link names, and you can edit every one of them.

How much AI can I use?

Each site can use AI to write steps 10 times a day, for free. After that, steps are written the plain way until the next day. Baton Pro removes the daily limit.

How do I add a “Take the tour” button?

In the Walkthroughs list, click “Copy tour link” under a published walkthrough. Put that link on any button or menu item. Only people in “Who sees it” get the tour.

Does Baton add any links?

Practice in your dashboard shows a small “Made with Baton” link in the top bar. Baton never adds links to the public side of your site.

Can I use it on the front end of my site?

Yes, with Baton Pro.
sections.changelog:
0.2.0

  • Practice on a safe copy: people click through screens exactly as you recorded them, and nothing they click there can break the site.
  • Publish, Install and Activate happen for real at the end, with the title and words they typed and the categories they ticked.
  • Watch it: sit back and see the walkthrough play itself, or play it again after the end.
  • Record inside Elementor with the Record with Baton button in its top bar (Baton Pro).
  • AI tidies recordings by leaving out side trips, and you can put them back.
  • After recording, Baton offers to remove the test posts and plugins it left behind.
  • Walkthroughs only go to people who can open every page in them.
  • “How was this?” at the end, and a Send feedback page to reach the author.
  • Each walkthrough’s size shows in the list.
  • Screen copies never keep passwords, keys, tokens or security codes.

0.1.0

  • First release: record dashboard walkthroughs, click-by-click guided tours on login, block editor support, previews, tour links, AI step writing.
